messages.author: f4249b01b99d0091
messages.subject: Re: Gradient colours with area
parts:
First, what's the 'medium' doing in scale_fill_gradient? I don't think
it's a parameter.

Second, if this were possible, you'd need a "fill=Value" inside the qplot call.

But third,
> Aesthetics can not vary with a ribbon

...geom_area (a ribbon) can't have varying aesthetics (like color).

Ben


On Fri, Aug 31, 2012 at 4:19 AM, Fabien Espic <fabien...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hello,
>
>
> I would like to use gradient colours with area. Quite a simple task but I
> cannot make it work unfortunately.
> This is an example:
> df <- data.frame(Date = as.Date(c("2008-01-01", "2009-01-01", "2010-01-01",
> "2011-01-01", "2012-01-01")), Value = c(0, 1, 0.5, -1, -2))
> I would like to achieve something like this:
> qplot(data = df, x = Date, y = Value) + geom_area() +
> scale_fill_gradient(low = "blue", medium = "yellow", high = "green")
>
> Can you help me with this?

messages.author: d34d025a513c07fc
messages.subject: Re: Gradient colours with area
parts:
On Mon, Sep 3, 2012 at 3:10 AM, Fabien Espic <fabien...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Thanks for the answer.
> The code I wrote was hypothetical. It was just meaning "for the medium
> values, use the color yellow".
>
> So there is no way to have an area with a gradient colour with ggplot2?

If what you want is a gradient within a geom_area, it's not possible
to do with ggplot2. ggplot2 is built on grid graphics, which I believe
doesn't support it.

-Winston
